body.p: Amendments in General

The title, abstract, and body of the specification have been amended for formality purposes. Claims 6 and 7 have been cancelled, and limitations substantially similar to those of claims 6 and 7 have been added to claim 1. Claims 1, 4, 5, and 9-18 have been amended for formality purposes and/or to better define the subject matter therein. No new matter has been added.
Specification Objections

The Office has objected to portions of the specification, including but not limited to the title and abstract. While Applicant does not necessarily agree, Applicant submits that these issues have been resolved by the amendments to the body of the specification, the title, and the abstract.
Claim Objections

The Office has objected to 1, 5, 7, 9, and 12-18 for alleged informalities. While Applicant does not necessarily agree, Applicant submits that these issues have been resolved by the amendments to the claims.

The Office has rejected claims 1-18 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. While Applicant does not necessarily agree, Applicant submits that these rejections are moot in light of the amendments to the claims.

Claims 1-18 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as being directed to a judicial exception, and more specifically, directed to an abstract idea. Applicant respectfully disagrees and requests that the Office reconsider, at least on the ground that the claims are integrated into a practical application under Step 2A, Prong
2 of the analysis.

As a threshold matter, the Office indicates on page 20 that "each of Claims 1 to 17 recites no additional elements and Claim 18 recites the additional elements of: a data processing unit and a control interface that is operationally connected to the data processing unit and includes a display module. These additional elements are generically recited computer elements." Applicant disagrees. Claims 1 to 17 recite at least the following additional elements:
(1) An exercise machine;
(2) Multimedia content;
(3) A control interface;
(4) A data processing unit;
(5) A display module.

These elements are integrally connected with the recited method steps. For instance, "dynamic[] modifying is performed on the data processing unit . . . to modify the control interface so that it assumes a respective operating configuration to display on the display module temporary controls representative of values selectable by the user." Moreover, "the step of dynamically modifying further comprises a step of indicating, by the data processing unit, based on the configuration instructions of the

exercise machine read together with the playing of the multimedia content, wherein it is indicated on the display module which of the temporary controls representative of values selectable by the user . . . is suggested by the personal trainer in the multimedia content."

These are not generic computer elements performing generic computer steps. These are steps that are being performed by physical components of a specifically practical machine - an exercise machine - to enhance the user experience and improve the exercise machine's overall functionality.

The Office cites the 2019 PEG for the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 101 but fails to provide any guidance from the 2019 PEG that actually supports the rejection. Indeed, the 2019 PEG actually supports the proposition that the claims are eligible under Step

2A, Prong 2, in Example 37 - Relocation of Icons on a Graphical User Interface. In that example, icons are rearranged on a graphical user interface (GUI) such that the most used icons are nearest the "start" icon of the computer system. There, the claim is eligible because "[t]he claim as a whole integrates the mental process into a practical application. Specifically, the additional elements recite a specific manner of automatically displaying icons to the user based on usage which provides a specific improvement over prior systems, resulting in an improved user interface for electronic devices." Such is the case here. As described above, the claimed method uses the exercise machine components to provide, through a display interface, an improved and enhanced experience. As such, any judicial exception is integrated into a practical application such that the claims are eligible.
Applicant submits that similar arguments apply to claim 18. For at least the above reasons, Applicant requests the withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 101.
Claims 1, 2, and 18 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0336827 to Intonato et al. (hereinafter "Intonato").
Claims 3-17 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Intonato in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0111318 to Evancha et al. (hereinafter "Evancha").
Claims 1 and 18 are independent claims from which all other claims depend, and as such the below arguments will focus upon these claims.

Claim 1 has been rejected as being anticipated by Intonato. Limitations substantially similar to those of claims 6 and 7 have been added to amended claim 1. Additionally, the claim has been amended to recite a method with "each of the temporary controls showing the corresponding value." Support for the amendments to claim 1 can be found, for example, in original claims 6 and 7, as well as FIGs. 5B-5D and pages 20, 23, and 24 of the specification as originally filed. For instance, the application as originally filed states:

values selectable by the user of at least one first
operating parameter P1 comprise:
a first temporary control Vii to select a first value
of the first operating parameter P1, e.g., a speed value

The application as filed also states on page 20 (emphasis

In an embodiment, in combination with any of the
preceding ones in which the user has selected a value of the at least one first operating parameter P1 and in

which an indication is provided on the display module 104 of which among the temporary controls CV-P1 representative of values selectable by the user of at least one first operating parameter P1 of the exercise machine 100 is suggested by the personal trainer in the multimedia content CM, the data processing unit 101, based on the configuration instructions IC read together
with the playing of the multimedia content CM.
Claims 6 and 7 were rejected as being obvious over Intonato in view of Evancha. Applicant respectfully disagrees and requests that the Office reconsider.

One objective of claim 1 is to provide a method for controlling a control interface of an exercise machine during consumption of multimedia content which allows the machine to be as intuitive, versatile, and simple as possible. This is achieved by making available to the user a plurality of temporary controls representative of values selectable by the user of at least one first operating parameter of the exercise machine, each of the temporary controls showing the corresponding value, wherein it is indicated on the display module which of the temporary controls representative of values selectable by the user of the at least one first operating parameter of the exercise machine is suggested by the personal trainer in the multimedia content for a phase of the set workout program that the user is performing in the set time interval that the multimedia content is at, which provides the user with all the selectable values plus the value as suggested

by the user to set up the exercise machine in a manner as intuitive, versatile and simple as possible. The user, even under stress or in presence of fatigue and/or excessive effort, is thus able to easily set up the machine, constituting a great improvement over the prior art.

A person of skill in the art would not come to the method of claim 1 based on Intonato and Evancha. This combination of references only provides the user with a single box with a value to be selected by the user. See, e.g., Intonato at FIG. 4, block 418; Evancha at FIG. 5, block 504. For instance, the block 418 in FIG. 4 of Evancha simply shows "jog", "run", and "sprint", without any indication of a corresponding value.

In addition, neither of Intonato and Evancha shows a plurality of values selectable by a user of a first operating parameter, each of them showing the corresponding value of the operating parameter, wherein an indication of the value as suggested by the personal trainer is provided on one of the temporary controls. The indication 409 "10 MIN EASY RUN" of FIG. 4 of Intonato and FIG. 4 of Evancha simply informs the user about the progression of the workout without any calculated suggestions to select one of the selectable operation mode of the treadmill (e.g. "jog", "run", or "sprint").

Furthermore, Intonato and Evancha teach add an additional single box with a value of a parameter to be selected by the user: block 418 of FIG. 5 of Intonato refers to a "6.0 MINUTE MILE PACE" and block 418 of FIG. 5 of Evancha refers to a "6.0 MINUTE MILE PACE." These are separate selections from the plurality of selectable operation modes of the treadmill such as "jog", "run", or "sprint," therefore creating a further difficulty for the user who has to move his gaze and does not have a view of the indication in the same place as the selectable operation modes.

There is therefore no teaching, suggestion, or motivation from the Intonato/Evancha combination to arrive at the method of claim 1. For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that the claim is non-obvious over the cited art, and requests the withdrawal of the rejection.
While different than claim 1, claim 18 has been amended in a similar manner, and Applicant submits that similar arguments apply. As such, Applicant requests the withdrawal of the claim 18 rejection.
Each of claims 2-17 depends from independent claim 1,
discussed above. As such, Applicant submits that each of these claims is also novel and non-obvious, and requests the withdrawal of the rejections.

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are unpatentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application.
Applicant submits that all claims pending herein are in condition for allowance and respectfully requests that a timely Notice of Allowance be issued in this case.
